appended_meaning:
The materially referenced needle-program conditions require a version-specific comparison, because the four requirements Acts do not print one identical rule or one common section number. The complete clauses are PL113-235 division G section 521 (2015), PL115-31 division H section 520 (2017), PL116-94 division A section 527 (2020), and PL117-328 division H section 526 (2023). Each uses funds appropriated in its own Act/division, with the established section 3 division-reference rule and express notwithstanding-any-other-provision language. Another version's section number is not substituted by number alone; each complete needle-program clause is selected in its own operative Title V.

The complete 2015 section 521 bars use of covered appropriated division funds to carry out any program of distributing sterile needles or syringes for hypodermic injection of any illegal drug. Its operative object is a distribution program, rather than only buying supplies. It does not print the later purchase-only wording or the later qualified other-program-elements proviso. Those later qualifications are not retroactively inserted into this source object, and its broader program wording is not silently copied into the three later objects. The adjacent rescission heading belongs to the following section 522 and is excluded by the exact original coordinate; no original glyph or operative clause is repaired.

The complete 2017, 2020 and 2023 clauses instead bar use of their covered appropriated division funds to purchase sterile needles or syringes for hypodermic injection of any illegal drug. Each separately provides that this limitation does not apply to spending for program elements other than making those purchases, only if the relevant State or local health department, in consultation with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, makes the specified jurisdiction-level determination and the program operates in accordance with State and local law. The determination is that the applicable State or local jurisdiction is experiencing, or is at risk for, a significant increase in hepatitis infections or an HIV outbreak due to injection drug use. Actual incidence and risk are alternatives; hepatitis increase and HIV outbreak are alternatives; the injection-drug-use nexus, CDC consultation and lawful-operation predicate remain. This proviso does not authorize the prohibited purchases, waive the required determination or cover every program merely because it provides medical services.

The three later clauses match at this complete operative extent, after a private comparison removes only their original notes, page markers and differing section labels. Their original source bytes, annotations, page markers, section numbers, division identities and dates remain unchanged. The 2015 rule is materially different and is recorded separately. Matching later clauses do not establish that all four conditions are identical, that one version repeals or overrides another incorporated reference, or that all source-year scopes apply identically to a current individual or grant. The literal eleven-authority continuing-conditions chain, its dated periods and amendment scopes, and the additional exact EH Division B 2101(d) authority remain preserved; full dated carry-forward application remains unfinished research.

These are requirements-source conditions within the already established health-transfer chain, not a new nationwide ban on private needle programs, a determination that any health department made a qualifying finding, an actual grant/service/coverage result, a new immigration eligibility condition or a finding of unlawful expenditure. No categorical program permission or prohibition is inferred for a particular medical recipient or trafficking-victim cohort. The member-neutral meaning remains context for the whole H.R. 1968 passage choice, without assigning a separate needle-policy stance, motive or four additional legislative actions to either member. Shared compacts, recorded choices, counting, eligibility and the compiled proposition graph remain unchanged.

This completes only the four selected needle-program clauses and their bounded version comparison. Other materially relevant program, HHS and general conditions, substantive cross-references, exact continuing/application review and the rest of the package remain executable research. Unfinished research is not unavailable evidence. All 70 separate application questions, including frozen Q68/Q69/Q70, remain unchanged. No full fund/package/domain closure, independent acceptance, production eligibility or publication is declared.

SEC. 3. <<NOTE: 1 USC 1 note.>> REFERENCES. Except as expressly provided otherwise, any reference to ``this Act'' contained in any division of this Act shall be treated as referring only to the provisions of that division. 

DIVISION G--DEPARTMENTS <<NOTE: Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2015. Department of Labor Appropriations Act, 2015.>> OF LABOR, HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, AND EDUCATION, AND RELATED AGENCIES APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2015 

Sec. 506. (a) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for any abortion. (b) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for health benefits coverage that includes coverage of abortion. (c) The term ``health benefits coverage'' means the package of services covered by a managed care provider or organization pursuant to a contract or other arrangement. Sec. 507. (a) The limitations established in the preceding section shall not apply to an abortion-- (1) if the pregnancy is the result of an act of rape or incest; or (2) in the case where a woman suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness, including a life-endangering physical condition caused by or arising from the pregnancy itself, that would, as certified by a physician, place the woman in danger of death unless an abortion is performed. (b) Nothing in the preceding section shall be construed as prohibiting the expenditure by a State, locality, entity, or private person of State, local, or private funds (other than a State's or locality's contribution of Medicaid matching funds). (c) Nothing in the preceding section shall be construed as restricting the ability of any managed care provider from offering abortion coverage or the ability of a State or locality to contract separately with such a provider for such coverage with State funds (other than a State's or locality's contribution of Medicaid matching funds). (d)(1) None of the funds made available in this Act may be made available to a Federal agency or program, or to a State or local government, if such agency, program, or government subjects any institutional or individual health care entity to discrimination on the basis that the health care entity does not provide, pay for, provide coverage of, or refer for abortions. (2) In this subsection, the term ``health care entity'' includes an individual physician or other health care professional, a hospital, a provider-sponsored organization, a health maintenance organization, a health insurance plan, or any other kind of health care facility, organization, or plan.
